findings.title: Cisco IOS XE web UI privilege escalation (creates admin account)
findings.description: An unauthenticated remote attacker can create a privilege-15 account through the HTTP/HTTPS web UI and take full control of the device. Release trains without a listed fix are reported as affected; confirm newer trains against the Cisco advisory.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to a fixed release (17.9.4a, 17.6.6a, 17.3.8a, 16.12.10a or later). Until then run 'no ip http server' and 'no ip http secure-server', and check for unknown local accounts.
evidence: IOS XE 17.06.04 is in the affected range
Affected feature enabled: ip http server

findings.title: Cisco IOS XE web UI command injection (root implant)
findings.description: Used together with CVE-2023-20198 to run commands as root and install an implant. Release trains without a listed fix are reported as affected; confirm newer trains against the Cisco advisory.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to a fixed release. Until then disable the HTTP/HTTPS server.
evidence: IOS XE 17.06.04 is in the affected range
Affected feature enabled: ip http server

findings.title: Plain HTTP management server enabled
findings.description: The HTTP server is unencrypted and has been the entry point for several critical IOS XE attacks.
findings.remediation: Run 'no ip http server'. If the web UI is needed, use 'ip http secure-server' restricted by an ACL.
evidence: ip http server

findings.title: ISR4331/K9 is end of sale; support is ending
findings.description: The model is no longer sold. Security fixes continue only until the vendor's last date of support.
findings.remediation: Add the device to the hardware refresh plan.
evidence: ISR 4331: end of sale; check Cisco's notice for the last date of support.

findings.title: Default SNMP community string
findings.description: 'public' and 'private' are the first values attackers try.
findings.remediation: Remove the default community and move to SNMPv3 (authPriv).
evidence: snmp-server community ****

findings.title: SNMP read-write community configured
findings.description: Anyone with the string can change the configuration.
findings.remediation: Remove RW communities; use SNMPv3 with read-only views for monitoring.
evidence: snmp-server community **** RW

findings.title: 'enable password' used instead of 'enable secret'
findings.description: The enable password is stored with weak, reversible encoding.
findings.remediation: Replace with 'enable secret' (type 8 or 9) and remove 'enable password'.
evidence: enable password

findings.title: 2811 is past vendor end of support
findings.description: The vendor no longer releases security fixes for this model, so new vulnerabilities on it will stay unpatched.
findings.remediation: Plan a hardware replacement. Until then, restrict management access to a dedicated management network.
evidence: Cisco 2800 series ISR: last date of support has passed. Confirm the date in Cisco's end-of-life notice.

findings.title: Cisco ASA web services read-only path traversal
findings.description: An unauthenticated remote attacker can read files from the web services file system when WebVPN or AnyConnect is configured.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to a fixed release for your train (e.g. 9.8.4.20, 9.12.3.12, 9.14.1.10 or later). Trains with no fix (9.7 and older than 9.6) need a move to a supported train.
evidence: ASA 9.8(4)15 is in the affected range
Affected feature enabled: webvpn

findings.title: ASDM/HTTPS management open to any address
findings.remediation: Restrict 'http <network> <mask> <interface>' to the management network.
evidence: http 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 outside

findings.title: Firewall rule permits any to any
findings.description: A permit-any rule removes the protection the firewall should give.
findings.remediation: Replace the rule with specific sources, destinations and services.
evidence: access-list dmz_out extended permit ip any any
